title: RAW soldering keeps a metal aid and alternative adjuncts distinct despite operation-specific material effects
summary: RAW UNREVIEWED. Complete Steele id00105 makes tin protective in fire but destructive of hammerability when mixed, then says named lead joints cannot be soon soldered without tin and cannot be soldered without grease or tallow. The proposed account retains the two aid classes, alternative scope, qualified soon and separate operation outcomes; it does not turn requirements into a sufficient recipe.

design.unit: Whole id00105, Tin in fire departeth metals of divers kind through Neither may these be soldered without grease or tallow. Full paragraph and all its attributed claims are mandatory, inside the already-owned whole chapter.
design.mechanism: One named material participates in different operations with different written effects. The final soldering cases attach a metal aid to the prompt/readily joining of lead with three named receivers, then attach a separate grease-or-tallow condition to those cases. This gives linked recipient, operation, adjunct and modal scopes rather than a single good/bad material value or an undifferentiated list of ingredients.
design.positive_consequence: An account that makes grease a substitute for tin loses the separately stated tin requirement; an account that requires grease AND tallow loses the source alternative; an account that lets tin alone guarantee a successful joint promotes necessary support to sufficiency. Applying the mixture-induced loss of hammerability to every fire-protection or soldering claim also changes the operation and property owner. A faithful full-content account must be able to keep these claims together without choosing one universal sign for tin.
design.meaning_anchor_needed: A later candidate must explicitly bind the repeated tin, lead and these referents to the named operations and distinguish the metal aid from the grease/tallow adjuncts, with written modal/alternative scope. These meanings may be proposed as exposed-data hypotheses, but material-name resemblance, shared affixes or an ingredient list alone do not supply the binding. No target counterpart is currently selected.
whole_source_duties: Opening: tin in fire separates metals, including lead/brass from gold/silver, and protects other metals in hot fire. Hard brass/iron nevertheless burn and waste in strong fire without tin. The source does not give temperatures, quantities or a controlled protocol.
Tinning brazen vessels is said to reduce rust venom and improve savour; tin also tempers mirrors and makes ceruse as lead does. These are mandatory full-paragraph claims, not modern use advice.

Aristotle-attributed composition uses good quicksilver and evil brimstone, not well mixed but joined in small parts, to explain silver colour without its sadness. Preserve the historical terminology; do not equate this automatically with modern density or purity.

Hermes-attributed alchemy says tin breaks all metals/bodies mixed with it because of its dryness and destroys hammer-work obedience. This is a different operation/property relation from protection in fire, not proof that tin is simply universally beneficial or harmful.

If quicksilver is mixed therewith, the next pronouns, crassing, initial whitening and later blackening/defilement must remain. The pronoun owners and crassing are not fully resolved in this edited wording; do not invent a precise alloy reaction or use it as an independently clear timed case.
Burnt tin produces red as lead does; strong fire is said to bring back the first matter of tin. This is not a demonstrated reversible chemical process or a quantity-conservation law.

The final comparison places tin more nesh than silver and harder than lead, yet lead may not be soon soldered to lead, brass or iron without tin. Retain soon: this is qualified facilitation/necessity, not unqualified physical impossibility.

Neither may these be soldered without grease or tallow. Preserve these as anaphoric to the named soldering cases, tin as a separate aid, and grease/tallow as the stated alternatives. Do not infer success or a complete sufficient recipe merely from presence of both aid classes.
rivals: All named ingredients are interchangeable alternatives; the text instead keeps tin separate from grease/tallow.
All prerequisites are jointly sufficient to cause successful soldering; no such full guarantee is written.
The absence of tin makes soldering absolutely impossible at any time; this drops soon.
Tin always protects or always destroys; the paragraph gives operation- and property-specific claims.
The whole chapter supplies a modern laboratory protocol, or the uncertain quicksilver pronouns can be silently resolved into one measured process.
